text:
Calgary won a game it was outplayed in, and the reason sits in the crease. Devin Cooley stopped 34 of 36 shots, and the shots Carolina took were good enough that an average goalie would have allowed about four. That is what goals saved above expected measures: Cooley kept out roughly two goals more than the chances deserved. Carolina's expected goals, a measure of chance quality, were 4.03 to 2.68, and in simulated replays of every shot the Hurricanes won 71 percent of the time. They lost 3-2 in regulation.

Carolina controlled the first period, out-chancing Calgary 1.69 to 0.37 in expected goals, but the scoring waited until the second. Jesperi Kotkaniemi opened it at 6:09. Matvei Gridin tied it at 18:30, and Morgan Frost put Calgary ahead on the power play at 19:39 with a tip-in. Jalen Chatfield answered 17 seconds later at 19:56 on a shot with a 1 percent chance of scoring, leaving it 2-2 after two.

The third period was Calgary's best, and the Flames edged the chance count 1.66 to 1.20. Yegor Sharangovich snapped home the winner at 15:32, set up by Frost and Jake Middleton. Matt Coronato had a 38 percent look later in the period, but Brandon Bussi stopped it. Calgary also won 33 of 58 faceoffs, and Cooley took first star.
